lemma: TARGET (not yet proved): a uniform refuter R for decision MCSP[s] at the CJSW Prop 4.3 thresholds is an algorithm that on input 1^n outputs y in {0,1}^N (N = 2^n) with y not in Im(Eval_{n,s}), in time poly(N) (or quasi-poly, per Prop 4.3 uniformity), for every admissible n. Three tasks are kept apart: (1) a counterexample to ONE given circuit (a single SAT call suffices); (2) a point outside Im(Eval_{n,s}) for fixed n (a finite search over the circuit family: exists-y forall-circuits); (3) the uniform asymptotic refuter of (2) for all n, with all resources counted.
gap: The FruitStack SAT generator solves task (1) and, for fixed n, task (2) only by enumerating the circuit family (2^{poly(s)} circuits), so it is not a uniform poly(N) refuter. Missing lemma G1: an algorithm producing a y outside Im(Eval_{n,s}) in time poly(N) for every n, or a proof that no such algorithm exists under known hypotheses. The CJSW Prop 4.3 proof step (Theorem 1.4 argument, small-circuit claim under P = NP) is still unread, so the arrow refuter => P != NP is not verified here.

proved_step: Counting lemma: for a basis of g binary ops, |Im_{n,s}| <= (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s. Hence for (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s < 2^N a random y in {0,1}^N avoids Im_{n,s} with probability >= 1 - (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s/2^N. Proof: a circuit with k gates is a sequence of k triples (op,i,j) with g*(n+s)^2 choices each; sum over k<=s.

gap: G1 unchanged. S0002 (counting lemma |Im_{n,s}| <= (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s) is an existence statement only: it gives a y outside Im for (s+1)(g(n+s)^2)^s < 2^N, found by random sampling. It is not a poly(N)-time construction and certifying y not in Im is itself an MCSP question. It is Shannon-type bookkeeping and does not count as progress on G1. Still open: (a) the threshold s of CJSW Prop 4.3 relative to the counting regime, (b) a deterministic poly(N) construction of y (range avoidance). Self-review not possible; S0002 needs review by another model family.
